title: SonicRoute
tagline: Send each app's audio to the device you choose.
intro: Play music through your speakers and keep games and calls in your headset. SonicRoute runs in the Windows system tray and lets you choose each app’s playback and recording devices. In the quick panel, Ctrl-click to add or remove an output, or Shift-click to select a range. All editions can play audio through multiple PC outputs at once. Full can also use outputs on a connected Android phone. Adjust the volume with hotkeys or the mouse wheel, and save routine changes as automation rules.

downloadIntro: Choose **Full** for Android audio, virtual displays and AirPlay, or **Lite** for PC audio only. Both have x64 and experimental ARM64 builds. **Legacy** is the PC-only x64 edition for systems using .NET Framework 4.8. The direct downloads below are for {release}. See the Microsoft Store listings for the versions of Full and Lite available there.
liteRequirement: One portable executable. Install the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime for the build’s architecture (x64 or ARM64).
legacyRequirement: Extract the ZIP and run SonicRoute. It uses Windows’ .NET Framework 4.8.
storeRequirement: The Store offers Full and Lite. Both require the x64 .NET 10 Desktop Runtime.
runtimeNote: For Full or Lite, install {runtime} for the architecture you downloaded. Legacy uses .NET Framework 4.8. Older builds that use {runtime8} are available in the archive and no longer receive updates.
steps: **Launch SonicRoute.** Run the downloaded EXE. If you use Legacy, fully extract the ZIP file first. Double-click the SonicRoute icon in the system tray to open the main window.

**Choose your devices.** In Settings, select the headphones and speakers you want to see in the quick panel. Click the tray icon once to open the panel. Expand an app’s row to select its output device, or drag its slider to adjust the volume.

**Use the mouse wheel.** Scroll over the SonicRoute icon to adjust the target app’s volume. Hold Alt while scrolling to change its output, or Shift to adjust the default output device’s volume. You can extend these controls to the entire system tray in Settings.
commandNote: The `sr` command sends a rule name or ID to a running copy of SonicRoute over a named pipe. Start SonicRoute once to register the command, then close and reopen your terminal. You can now call `sr` from a script, AutoHotkey or Stream Deck. If SonicRoute is closed, `sr` returns an error. See {faq}.

releaseSummary:
Full can now receive AirPlay audio (PCM, ALAC, AAC-LC and AAC-ELD) and mirror a screen at its original aspect ratio using a receiver written in C#. Set an optional pairing code, keep the mirror on top or press F11 for full screen. Drag audio to a PC output, an Android phone’s speaker or a Bluetooth device connected to the phone. Android and AirPlay support H.265 (HEVC). Android falls back to H.264 if the encoder cannot start. You can choose Android audio and video decoders. SonicRoute checks the available encoders when you open the device settings and sends gamepad input only to the focused video window.

Android pairing now puts the QR code (refreshed every two minutes) beside the manual pairing code. Reconnecting or refreshing a device checks its identity and looks for its current address and port on the local network. SonicRoute preserves a manually entered address if the search fails and can restore settings for a previously paired device.

All editions now have separate options to keep the mic indicator on screen when all microphones are muted or when the default recording device is muted. Configuration tools share one row. Long app lists render only the visible rows once the list exceeds 20 entries. SonicRoute combines on-screen updates and frees decoded PNG source data, backs up settings to `config.json.bak` and records diagnostics when errors occur. Full also releases unused video textures and leaves garbage collection to the runtime when a window closes. Lite is available separately in the Microsoft Store, and all editions include an offline copy of the GPL-3.0-only license. See {history} for details.

features: **Choose playback and recording devices for each app.** Send game audio to your headset and use its microphone for voice chat. In the quick panel, Ctrl-click a playback device to add it to or remove it from the selection. Shift-click to select a range. All editions can play audio on several PC outputs at once. Full can also include available Android phone outputs. Windows remembers each app’s primary PC output and recording device after SonicRoute exits. Playback on additional outputs requires SonicRoute to be running.

**Control the current app with the mouse wheel.** By default, SonicRoute prioritizes the most recently used foreground app with an audio session. Scroll over the tray icon to adjust its volume, or hold Alt while scrolling to switch its output. On-screen indicators (OSD) show the result, and a global hotkey lets you toggle microphone mute.

**See which apps are playing audio.** The quick panel has a volume slider and a live level meter for each app. It remembers its position, and you can set its height from 350 to 850 device-independent pixels.

**Connect an Android device or use AirPlay (Full).** Play Android app audio on the PC, open apps in separate virtual display windows, or send PC audio back to the phone. Android supports H.265 video and gamepad input in the active video window. The built-in C# AirPlay receiver plays audio and mirrors the screen at its original aspect ratio. Use the quick panel to send audio to a PC output, an Android phone’s speaker or a Bluetooth device connected to the phone. Smart Volume evens out loud passages on supported streams. In development builds of Full, you can send audio from Android to the PC using Opus (the default) or uncompressed PCM. Set the latency mode to Ultra-low latency, Balanced (the default), or Stable. Each phone’s settings take effect the next time you start an audio stream from it. When the Android encoder supports it, SonicRoute adjusts the virtual display’s video bitrate as connection conditions change.

**Run rules from an event or the command line.** Choose from 6 triggers and 39 actions. Trigger a rule with a hotkey, on a schedule, when an app opens, closes or gains focus, or when SonicRoute starts. Chain actions to switch devices, set volume, mute audio, open a program or file, or run PowerShell. Scripts and hardware controllers can run a rule with `sr` through the existing SonicRoute process.

**Respond to Windows events.** SonicRoute uses system notifications, checks process state once a second when needed, and releases data it no longer needs. All three editions support nine interface languages. Lite and Legacy focus on PC audio.

useCaseActions: Adjust voice chat (such as Discord) without changing the game’s volume. You can also send the game and the chat to different outputs.
Send music to your speakers and keep the game in your headset. Scroll over the SonicRoute icon to adjust the target app’s volume, or hold Alt and scroll to switch its output.
Create a rule that switches to the headset, sets the volume to 40% and opens voice chat when the game starts. Use an exit rule to switch back to the speakers.
The default shortcut, Ctrl+Shift+N, toggles mute for all microphones. Enable the persistent on-screen indicator to see when they’re muted.
Send the apps you want to record to a separate physical or virtual output, then select that output in your recording software. Leave chats and notifications on another output.

In Full, route Android audio to the PC and use phone apps in a virtual display. You can also receive AirPlay audio and screen mirroring. Use the quick panel to play the audio on a PC output, an Android phone’s speaker or a Bluetooth device connected to the phone.
commandSnippetComment: Trigger an automation rule (SonicRoute must be running)
faqQuestions: What happens to app routing and volume when I exit SonicRoute?
How much CPU or battery does SonicRoute use in the background?
faqAnswers: Windows keeps each app’s primary PC playback device, recording device and the volume of existing audio sessions. Playback on additional outputs stops when you exit SonicRoute. Keep SonicRoute running to use hotkeys, tray controls, automation, phone audio, screen mirroring or clipboard sync.

Full and Lite require the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime for the build’s architecture. The Store editions require the x64 runtime. Legacy uses .NET Framework 4.8. Archived .NET 8 builds are still available but no longer receive updates.

SonicRoute relies on Windows notifications and checks process state once a second when needed. It releases data it no longer uses. CPU use and battery impact depend on your system and what you’re doing.
